newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-May 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-May 22.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- Chinese Vice-Premier Qian Qichen said the Preparatory Committee, which set up the mechanism for Hong Kong's handover to China, need not be disbanded for the time being but would cease operating from July 1.

-- Publishers of a Chinese-language magazine which started as an underground publication on the mainland and moved overseas after the Tiananmen massacre in 1989 plan to distribute it in Hong Kong to try to reach more mainland readers after the handover.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Beijing issued orders banning state enterprises from buying and selling stocks. Market analysts believe the ban might affect the share prices of red chips -- Hong Kong-incorporated companies with financial backing from China -- in the territory.

-- TA KUNG PAO -- At an international conference in the Philippines, Chinese Vice-Premier Li Lanqing stressed Beijing would give full support to Hong Kong's future development and said people from all over the world were welcome to develop their businesses in the territory.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- The Hong Kong stock exchange and the Securities and Futures Commission threatened to use their full powers to curb the recent spate of unusual share price and turnover movements in listed companies.

-- Stock exchange executives met with the senior management of Beijing Enterprises, the proposed listed arm of the Beijing municipal government, to express their concern over how its $2.9 billion initial public offering had been handled.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Chief Justice-designate Andrew Li was warned that a failure by judiciary chiefs to come to grips with the concept of "one system, two languages" was threatening havoc in the courts.
